title: Production Readiness Review: Is This Service Ready to Launch?
intro: Before an SRE team at Google agrees to support a service, it goes through a Production Readiness Review: a checklist of things that separate 'it works' from 'it survives production'. Here you check a new service, loyalty, in namespace shop against the essentials, using nothing but kubectl and promtool.

steps.prompt: Redundancy: check the loyalty deployment's replica count and which nodes its pods run on (label app=loyalty, namespace shop).
expected_commands: kubectl get pods -n shop -l app=loyalty -o wide
kubectl get po -n shop -l app=loyalty -o wide
steps.fake_output:
NAME                       READY   STATUS    NODE
loyalty-7b8c9d6f5-a1b2c    1/1     Running   node-1
loyalty-7b8c9d6f5-d3e4f    1/1     Running   node-1
steps.explanation: Two replicas, both on node-1, so one node failure takes the service down.
steps.why: Replicas only help if they fail independently. Topology spread constraints (or pod anti-affinity) across nodes and zones are a standard readiness item, and a very common gap.

steps.prompt: Health checks: show the loyalty deployment's readiness and liveness probes.
expected_commands: kubectl get deploy loyalty -n shop -o yaml | grep -A5 Probe
steps.fake_output: (none: no readiness or liveness probe is defined)
steps.explanation: No probes: Kubernetes sends traffic to pods that aren't ready, and never restarts a hung one.
steps.why: Without readiness probes, every deploy and restart sends traffic to pods that are still starting, which means errors on every rollout. tutorial-021 covers probe design; the key rule is that readiness checks only what this pod needs, never shared downstreams (sre-tutorial-009).

steps.prompt: Safe maintenance: check whether loyalty has a PodDisruptionBudget in shop.
steps.fake_output:
NAME           MIN AVAILABLE   MAX UNAVAILABLE   ALLOWED DISRUPTIONS
checkout-pdb   N/A             1                 1
cart-pdb       N/A             1                 1
steps.why: Without one, a node drain for patching can evict both replicas at once. Use maxUnavailable: 1 rather than a minAvailable equal to the replica count, which blocks drains forever (incident-012).

steps.prompt: Resource sizing: check the loyalty container's requests and limits.
steps.explanation: No requests or limits at all.
steps.why: Without requests the scheduler can't place the pods sensibly, and they're the first evicted under memory pressure (BestEffort QoS). Without a memory limit, a leak can starve its neighbours (sre-incident-005). Set requests from load-test data (sre-tutorial-005).

steps.prompt: Monitoring: check that loyalty has alerting rules, by validating the team's rules file alerts/loyalty.yml.
steps.fake_output:
Checking alerts/loyalty.yml
  FAILED:
open alerts/loyalty.yml: no such file or directory
steps.explanation: There are no alerts, so nobody gets paged when loyalty breaks.
steps.why: A service isn't ready until someone gets paged when it breaks, ideally on SLO burn rate (monitoring-tutorial-012), with a runbook linked from the alert. Add redundancy, probes, a PDB, resources, and alerts, and this service passes the review.
